item.title: Talocrural Posterior Talar Glide
clinicalUse: Limited dorsiflexion after healed ankle sprain
patientPosition: Supine or long sitting with ankle near neutral and heel supported.
therapistPosition: Stand at foot end or beside ankle.
contact: Broad contact over anterior talus/neck of talus without compressing dorsalis pedis region excessively.
forceDirection: Posterior glide of talus relative to tibia/fibula.
Rhythmic Maitland oscillation or sustained glide depending on chosen approach.
steps: 6. Add calf raise, squat and balance work.
mistakes: Pulling foot without true talar glide.
safety: Avoid with fracture, acute syndesmotic instability or severe swelling requiring further assessment.
item.visualCue: Tibia fixed → Talus glides posteriorly → Dorsiflexion/lunge re-test.

subTechniques.name: Posterior Talar Glide for Dorsiflexion
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve ankle dorsiflexion when posterior talar glide is restricted.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine/long sitting or weight-bearing depending on the technique. Keep the foot close to neutral and the tibia controlled.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the distal tibia/fibula. Use a broad contact over the anterior talus/neck of talus without compressing the dorsalis-pedis region.
subTechniques.direction: Glide the talus posteriorly relative to the mortise using the selected Maitland grade.
subTechniques.reassess: Weight-bearing lunge distance, squat and gait.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Measure the weight-bearing lunge before and after—the change should be obvious enough to justify keeping the technique.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid acute syndesmotic instability or fracture.

subTechniques.name: Anterior Talar Glide for Plantarflexion
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve plantarflexion when anterior talar glide is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Prone or supine with the ankle supported and the leg relaxed.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the distal tibia/fibula and contact the posterior talus/calcaneal region in a way that avoids Achilles compression.
subTechniques.direction: Guide the talus anteriorly in a controlled oscillatory glide.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Confirm that the limitation is talocrural rather than simply soft-tissue or pain-limited.
